title: De Proprietatibus Rerum - Medieval Manuscript
shelf_note: A Gothic textualis manuscript of Bartholomaeus Anglicus, with rubricated and blue initials and paraphs. It belongs in the Smithsonian collection, and a late-13th/14th-century date fits the hand.
structure_note: The counts disagree: structure.pages_translated is 0, but pages_translated_field is 511 and this page carries a translation, so the instruments disagree (E2). The 130 backsteps and 177 repeats among 336 printed numbers are far too many for a clean sequence. The likely cause is the <page-num> tag picking up a mix of the later-hand folio numbers and the marginal reference numerals (like the '80' and '81' on this leaf), plus misreads. Here the OCR's <page-num>208 sits on a leaf whose top right reads '209'. This looks like a furniture-tagging problem (O11), not a splice.

pages.layout: two columns of Gothic textualis; red-and-blue running head 'XIX'; red/blue flourished initials and a run of red/blue paraphs in column b; later-hand numerals '80' and '81' in the margins and a later-hand marginal note at right

tr_errors.english: A good odor is so constituted, and so subtle in substance, that once its lightness has dissolved it, it is able to make its way to the brain.
tr_errors.problem: the fluent English is reconstructed from the image or from knowledge of the text, not from the transcription beside it. The broad sense matches the leaf where I can check it (musk, roses in hot water, the nipple-shaped caruncles in the nostrils, Ylaoch, Galen). The <meta> does warn that 'many words are uncertain', so the reader is told.

tr_errors.english: They saw that some things, such as pepper, have no odor and yet are hot and sharp, and that some things smell sweet in part.
tr_errors.problem: the image appears to contrast cold things that are fragrant (roses) with hot things that have no odour (pepper), and then says that they thought a thing could not be known at all by its odours. The English drops the cold/fragrant half and invents 'some things smell sweet in part'.

other.note: raw markup in the reader text: '<column-break/>', '->¶ ... <-' centring arrows on ten lines, '<margin>80</margin>' and '<margin>81</margin>'
the running head 'XIX' is promoted to a heading, '# BOOK XIX', in the middle of the book

missing.english: odor is a property perceptible by smell, as Ylaoch says
missing.why: 'Ylaoch' is a medieval corruption of Isaac (Isaac Israeli, Isaac Judaeus), the cited authority; a general reader cannot identify him

missing.english: infects the air and likewise the animal spirit, which it corrupts
missing.why: 'animal spirit' (spiritus animalis) is a technical term of Galenic physiology, not 'spirit' in the everyday sense

missing.english: By its heat it dissolves humor and restrains flux and motion.
missing.why: 'humor' is the four-humour theory of the body and needs a short gloss

book_verdict: This is the right leaf of a genuine Bartholomaeus manuscript, but the transcription is mostly unreadable non-words. The fluent English was evidently made from the image or from knowledge of the text, and it drops or invents at least one clause. An expert would also see the raw markup and the 'BOOK XIX' heading at once.
